_about: Hobart public holidays, used when the data.gov.au dataset cannot supply a year.
In practice this is not a fallback but the source. The national dataset —
'Australian Public Holidays Dates Machine Readable Dataset' — is titled
[INACTIVE] and its newest resource is 2025, so it has nothing for 2026 or
2027 and no successor dataset exists on data.gov.au. The fetch is still
tried first, and will start winning if a year is ever published.
DERIVED, NOT SOURCED. These dates are worked out from the published rules
and from the convention the national dataset itself used in 2021-2023,
not read off an official 2026/2027 list. They should be checked against
the Tasmanian source before this is relied on. The rules applied:
- Royal Hobart Regatta is the second Monday in February. It is a
southern-Tasmania holiday and has never appeared in the national
dataset's tas rows, so it is added by us rather than filtered in.
- Eight Hours Day is the second Monday in March.
- King's Birthday is the second Monday in June.
- Good Friday, Easter Monday and Easter Tuesday follow the computus.
- ANZAC Day is NOT moved when it falls on a weekend. Confirmed from the
dataset: 25 April 2021 was a Sunday and carries no additional day.
- Christmas and Boxing Day keep their own dates when they fall on a
weekend, and an extra holiday is added afterwards, named
'(additional day)'. Confirmed from 2021 (Sat/Sun -> Mon and Tue) and
2022 (Sun/Mon -> Tue).
- Recreation Day (first Monday in November) is northern Tasmania and is
not here. It is also excluded in code, in case another source has it.
Easter Tuesday is a public holiday for the Tasmanian State Service only.
It is kept, because the hospitals' lists are affected by who is in, and
marked in the title rather than treated as a day off.
